text:
Andrew Copp has been one of the few Red Wings forwards producing lately, which is exactly what The Hockey News wrote on November 20: "Andrew Copp Stepping Up as Nearly All Red Wings Forwards Struggle." He has 8 points in his last ten games, 7 of them assists, while playing 19 to 21 minutes most nights. Detroit's offense has been thin enough that a 32-year-old two-way center is carrying a bigger share than anyone planned.

The rest of the line is less flattering. Three goals on 4.8 expected goals (the quality of chances), 8.6% shooting, and Detroit takes 45.8% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, 4.6 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey also flagged that his 2025-26 results ran ahead of his chances, so last season's 43 points were a little generous.

What Copp still does well is move the puck. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting with possession 62% of the time and 85th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season. He's the setup man on a team that badly needs finishers.
